body:
### What happens?

I am using duckDB to to read and write some parquet files. In the read path, I download the parquet file, load the existing data into a table, append rows to it and then export it to S3 over httpfs. Recently duckDB has been failing to read some files due to "Constraint Error: NOT NULL constraint failed: <column_name>". This is because the table in the application code that loads data from these files has "NOT NULL" constraint set for some columns and these files had NULL values in those columns. No one else is writing to (or reading from) these files apart from duckDB. These files are now corrupted and duckDB can no longer read or write to them. So looks like at some point duckDB was able to write NULL values to columns that were not supposed to hold NULL and saved them to S3. 

Looking at the logs, there were some 503s from S3 when duckDB tried to write to S3 and soon after these "null constraint" errors started showing up (the files got corrupted).

Looks like duckDB might be saving "partial data" when uploads to S3 are throttled and `COPY table_name TO 's3://s3-bucket/filename.parquet';` may violet constraints if the copy is throttled midway.

I don't know the details of how duckDB exports the table/file to S3 though (e.g. in chunks) - couldn't find any information on that. 

### To Reproduce

```
CREATE TABLE students (name VARCHAR NOT NULL);
COPY students TO 's3://s3-bucket/filename.parquet';
```
